item.title: Suspect in custody over destruction of Lord Ganesh statue in Ba
item.description: A suspect is in custody following the destruction of a Lord Ganesh statue at the Shri Maha Devi Gangaman Temple in Field 28, Rarawai, Ba. Police have confirmed the suspect is the same person arrested in Nadi earlier this year for allegedly committing a similar offence.
item.content:encoded:
A suspect is in custody following the destruction of a Lord Ganesh statue at the Shri Maha Devi Gangaman Temple in Field 28, Rarawai, Ba.

Police have confirmed the suspect is the same person arrested in Nadi earlier this year for allegedly committing a similar offence.

Police say a report was lodged in Ba and an investigation was conducted, leading to the suspect being taken into custody.

The alleged incident happened just days before Diwali, leaving the temple committee and the wider community devastated.

Temple Manager Munen Lingam says the temple committee discovered yesterday morning that the main Lord Ganesh statue was missing from its place, with the caretaker later finding pieces of the one-metre-high statue near a sacred fig tree.

Lingam says the statue had been broken against a stone, with some pieces placed in a sack and others thrown into a nearby creek.

He says this is the second time the temple has been targeted, following an incident in November when a Lord Hanuman statue was damaged and stolen.

Lingam says security at the temple had been strengthened following the previous incident, with additional grills and shutters installed, and plans to install CCTV cameras.

However, he says those responsible managed to cut the lock and damage the grill protecting the Lord Ganesh statue before destroying it.

Lingam says nothing else was stolen or damaged during the latest incident, and the small amount of money left by devotees at the temple was untouched.

He says the incident has deeply affected the temple committee, Ramayan Mandali and families from Field 28 and surrounding communities, particularly as devotees regularly gather there for prayers and religious activities.

Lingam says the community had been preparing for its Diwali celebrations, including a programme scheduled for Saturday, and many are now struggling to understand why the incident happened.

He says the community does not want the incident to create divisions between religions or races.

item.title: Government has not been sitting idly amid prolonged dry weather – Rabuka
item.description: Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka says the Government has not been sitting idly in responding to the challenges caused by prolonged dry weather conditions. In a statement, Rabuka says that for months, the Government has been warning about the impact of El Niño.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka says the Government has not been sitting idly in responding to the challenges caused by prolonged dry weather conditions.

In a statement, Rabuka says that for months, the Government has been warning about the impact of El Niño.

He says the Government has also been raising Fiji's concerns at international climate conferences, including COP, and calling on the world's major economies to recognise the challenges faced by small island nations like Fiji.

Rabuka says the Government has repeatedly warned that climate change is not a distant threat.

He further says its consequences are already being felt by people across Fiji, with communities experiencing water shortages.

The Prime Minister says he understands the difficulties this is causing families, farmers and businesses.

He adds that the Water Authority of Fiji has been working every day to maintain water supplies and deliver water to affected communities.

Rabuka says that according to the latest figures presented to Parliament, 67 water trucks have been deployed.

He says more than 885,000 litres of water have been delivered by road since 30th October, while another 810,000 litres were delivered by sea between 30th September and 30th October.

He says disaster management teams, regional development officials and other Government agencies have also been responding, coordinating assistance and preparing for conditions that may become more difficult in the months ahead.

The Prime Minister says the Government has been preparing for this situation for months and will continue to strengthen its response as necessary.

Rabuka adds that the scale of the drought is serious, and while the Government cannot control the weather or make it rain, it can prepare, mobilise resources and do everything possible to protect the people.

He says this is also why the Government continues to advocate internationally for greater climate financing and assistance.

The Prime Minister says small countries like Fiji cannot be expected to carry the growing burden of climate change alone.

Rabuka says the international community needs to recognise what people in Fiji are experiencing and support the country's efforts to build resilience.

He further says some may choose to take his words out of context and use them to score political points, and they are free to do so.

However, he says that while others debate his words, Government teams are out there delivering water and helping communities.

Rabuka says this is a difficult period for the country, and it calls for solidarity, cooperation and a shared determination to look after one another.

He says Fiji will get through this together.

item.title: Qereqeretabua stresses she will vote against Constitution Bill according to NFP's directive
item.description: Assistant Minister for Foreign Affairs and National Federation Party MP, Lenora Qereqeretabua has made it clear that she will be voting against the Constitution Amendment Bill at its third reading, in accordance with the NFP’s directive. In a statement sent to fijivillage News, Qereqeretabua says her position has not changed.
item.content:encoded:
Assistant Minister for Foreign Affairs and National Federation Party MP, Lenora Qereqeretabua has made it clear that she will be voting against the Constitution Amendment Bill at its third reading, in accordance with the NFP’s directive.

In a statement sent to fijivillage News, Qereqeretabua says her position has not changed.

She says she remains committed to the NFP’s decision and will act accordingly when the Bill comes before Parliament.

In an interview with fijivillage News earlier this week, Qereqeretabua said the party believes more time is needed to consider the proposed Constitution Bill.

She said the process should not be rushed, arguing that Fiji should not replace a Constitution imposed on the country by imposing another without allowing sufficient time for proper consideration.

item.title: Style Fiji funding to strengthen support for people living with HIV and persons with disabilities
item.description: People living with HIV continue to face challenges accessing healthcare, with some struggling to afford bus fares to attend clinic appointments, while others face stigma and discrimination. This is one of the key concerns highlighted by Fiji Network Plus, as it receives support from Style Fiji to strengthen its care, counselling and support programmes.
item.content:encoded:
People living with HIV continue to face challenges accessing healthcare, with some struggling to afford bus fares to attend clinic appointments, while others face stigma and discrimination.

This is one of the key concerns highlighted by Fiji Network Plus, as it receives support from Style Fiji to strengthen its care, counselling and support programmes.

While speaking with fijivillage News, Fiji Network Plus representative Joeli Colati says while healthcare services may be available, the cost of getting to clinics and meeting daily needs remains a major challenge for many people living with HIV.

Colati says some people struggle to afford bus fares to attend their appointments, while others face difficulties putting food on the table or are afraid to seek healthcare because of stigma and discrimination.

He says being selected as one of Style Fiji's beneficiaries for 2026 means a lot to the organisation, as the funding will support its peer counselling, care and support programmes.

Its services include peer-to-peer counselling, treatment support, home visits, transport assistance and support for mothers living with HIV.

Colati says the organisation also works with the National HIV Response to improve access to HIV services across the country.

He says efforts are underway to decentralise HIV services to sub-divisional and divisional hospitals, with the aim of eventually making these services available at health centres.

Colati says healthcare professionals are also being trained to provide HIV services, particularly testing, which can deliver results within 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, Fiji Mobility Alliance, formerly known as the Spinal Injury Association, is also benefiting from Style Fiji's fundraising efforts.

Fiji Mobility Alliance representative Jay Nasilasila says the organisation has been operating for more than 10 years and was rebranded last year to better represent people with different types of physical impairments.

He says the organisation advocates for inclusivity and accessibility while providing free mobility devices to its members.

Nasilasila says the organisation receives two containers of mobility equipment annually from the United Kingdom through its partner, Fisher Net.

The equipment includes wheelchairs, elbow crutches, shower chairs, commode chairs and different types of walking aids.

He says funding received through last year's Style Fiji initiative has helped the organisation pay for the transportation of the containers into Fiji, allowing it to continue distributing mobility equipment to members free of charge.

Insert: Nasilasila on support 6th Nov 26

Nasilasila stresses that mobility devices cannot simply be handed out without proper assessment, as technicians must first assess individuals to ensure they receive the correct assistive equipment for their needs

He says the organisation also continues to advocate for accessible healthcare services, particularly for members who regularly visit health facilities and depend on medical consumables.

Both organisations have thanked the Style Fiji chairperson, committee, sponsors, donors and supporters for their continued assistance.

Fiji Network Plus will also showcase its services at the Style Fiji Market Day tomorrow, inviting members of the public, including hotel workers around Sheraton, to visit its booth and learn more about its work.

Style Fiji is marking its 15th anniversary this year, c ontinuing its efforts to raise funds through fashion and entertainment to support charitable organisations and communities in Fiji.
